Once upon a time there was a kind Shoemaker named Hans.
He made good shoes, but he was very poor.
One evening he had leather for only one more pair of shoes.
I will cut the leather tonight and sew it in the morning,
said Hans, and he went to bed.
In the morning Hans came into his workshop.
On the table stood a pair of shoes, neatly stitched.
Look, Greta,
said Hans.
Who could have made them?
They are the finest shoes I have ever seen,
said Greta.
That very day a rich man came into the shop.
He liked the shoes so much that he paid more than the usual price.
Now Hans had enough money to buy leather for two more pairs of shoes.
He cut out the leather and left it on the table.
Again the next morning the shoes were ready, sewn with tiny, perfect stitches.
Again they sold at once, and Hans bought leather for four pairs.
Night after night the shoes appeared, and soon the shop was full of happy customers.
Just before Christmas Hans spoke to his wife.
Greta, let us stay up tonight and see who is helping us,
What a good idea,
They hid behind a curtain and waited.
At midnight two tiny elves came skipping in.
They had no clothes, only ragged scraps.
They sat at the table and began to stitch and hammer, quick as lightning.
Tap, tap, tap!
said Nib.
Stitch, stitch, stitch!
said Nob.
When all the shoes were finished, the elves ran away.
Those elves have made us rich,
Let us make them something to say thank you.
I will sew them little shirts and trousers.
And I will make them each a pair of tiny shoes,
On Christmas Eve they laid the gifts on the table.
At midnight the elves came skipping in, and they found the clothes.
Oh, how fine we look!
Now we need not work any more,
They danced out of the door and never came back, but Hans and Greta were happy for the rest of their lives.
